newsitem.title: CHINA: HK mortgage rate rise seen having limited impact.
newsitem.headline: HK mortgage rate rise seen having limited impact.

text.p: Hong Kong's property stocks tumbled on Tuesday after two major banks raised their mortgage rates prompting fears of a slump in housing demand, but analysts said the rise would not hurt property prices significantly.

"We don't expect the impact to be a major one. Potentially, I think this is basically going to hurt sentiment but demand for property is still very strong from genuine end-users," Merrill Lynch analyst Carol Lai said.

Hongkong Bank and Standard Chartered Bank raised their basic mortgage lending rates by 25 basis points to 9.25 percent recently. Analysts said the decision was in response to the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's worries about banks' exposure to the property market.

Property stocks led Hong Kong's blue-chip Hang Seng index lower on Tuesday with shares in Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd tumbling HK$2.00 to HK$100.00 and Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd falling HK$1.50 to HK$92.25.
New World Development Co Ltd slid HK$1.00 to HK$56.50 and Henderson Land Development Co Ltd dropped HK$1.00 to HK$70.50.
"The rise in mortgage lending rates gives a clear signal to the market that banks will tighten up credit policy to public buyers," said Philip Chan, an analyst at Yamaichi International.
"It gives a signal that competition in the banking sector on mortgage loans is finished and banks will start to look at profit margins," he said.

Ricky Tam, senior research manager at Delta Asia Securities, said end-users were now dominating the property market with speculators on the sidelines due to fears that the government may impose punitive measures against property speculators.

"But the increase in mortgage rates means (property) buyers will stay on the sidelines so that is hurting the market," he said. While a 25-basis-point rise should not prevent end-user demand, buyers may take a more wait-and-see approach, he added.

"Our view is still very much that the SAR (Special Administrative Region) government intends to limit the volatility in residential property prices by reducing excessive levels of speculation while also increasing home ownership levels," Merrill said in a report issued on Monday.
"We do not believe that the government wishes (or plans) to significantly undermine the property market in Hong Kong."

Lai said she expected property prices to continue consolidating over coming months after softening following the government's announcement last month of plans to increase land supply. Prices rose more than 30 percent during the first half of this year and are up 15 to 20 percent year to date, she said.
"There is very clear end-user demand for housing going forward," Lai said, adding that she expected 10 to 15 percent price growth over the next 12 to 18 months.
Adam Osborn, deputy head of research at BZW Asia, said of more concern in the stock market on Tuesday was a rising U.S. long bond yield.

With a slew of U.S. economic data due later this week ahead of the U.S. Federal Reserve's policy-setting meeting next Tuesday, investors were getting nervous about the direction of interest rates, brokers said.

"Going forward, we are going to say that the mortgage rates will change if you actually have a change in interest rates in Hong Kong and we are not forecasting that to happen before the end of the year," said Osborn.
